name: LLM Model and Profile Selector Components
description:
Here's a 5-line summary:

1. A reusable `Selector.vue` component was created supporting both single and multi-select modes with avatar display, text filtering, and alphabetical sorting.
2. Wrapper components `ChatLLMModelSelector.vue` and `ChatProfileSelector.vue` were built on top of `Selector.vue` for LLM model and profile selection respectively.
3. The selectors were initially placed above the textarea in `ChatInputBox.vue`, then moved into `ChatInputToolbar.vue` to save vertical space.
4. Layout issues were fixed by making selectors full-width with `flex-1` and `w-full` classes, with badge overflow capped at 1 visible item plus a count indicator.
5. The LLM model selector was enhanced to support toggle-deselect behavior, showing a `"default"` ghost badge when no model is selected, and scroll was added to the dropdown grid to handle large option lists.

<script setup>
import Selector from './Selector.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <Selector
    :items="profiles"
    :selected-items="selectedProfiles"
    label="Profiles"
    icon="fa-solid fa-plus"
    :is-single-select="false"
    @update:selected-items="onProfilesSelected"
  />
</template>

<script>
export default {
  props: {
    profiles: {
      type: Array,
      default: () => []
    },
    selectedProfiles: {
      type: Array,
      default: () => []
    }
  },
  emits: ['update:selected-profiles'],
  methods: {
    onProfilesSelected(selectedItems) {
      this.$emit('update:selected-profiles', selectedItems)
    }
  }
}
</script>

<script setup>
import Selector from './Selector.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <Selector
    :items="formattedModels"
    :selected-items="selectedModelItem"
    label="Model"
    icon="fa-solid fa-brain"
    :is-single-select="true"
    @update:selected-items="onModelSelected"
  />
</template>

<script>
export default {
  props: {
    selectedModel: String,
    models: {
      type: Array,
      default: () => []
    }
  },
  emits: ['model-changed'],
  computed: {
    formattedModels() {
      return (this.models || []).map(model => ({
        name: model.name,
        description: model.ai_model || model.description,
        avatar: null
      }))
    },
    selectedModelItem() {
      if (!this.selectedModel) return []
      const model = this.formattedModels.find(m => m.name === this.selectedModel)
      return model ? [model] : []
    }
  },
  methods: {
    onModelSelected(selectedItems) {
      const modelName = selectedItems.length > 0 ? selectedItems[0].name : ''
      this.$emit('model-changed', modelName)
    }
  }
}
</script>

# Summary

The user requested a refactor of the LLM model selector in a Vue.js chat application to match the profile selector pattern. The implementation created a reusable `Selector.vue` component supporting both single and multiple selection modes, with alphabetical sorting and real-time text filtering capabilities. The LLM model selector was moved from the toolbar to the chat input area, positioned before the profile selector, using the new unified selector component. All components were built following the VueDeveloper profile structure with TailwindCSS and DaisyUI, eliminating code duplication through component reuse.

# Summary

1. **Created a unified `Selector.vue` component** - A reusable single/multiple selection component with alphabetical sorting, text filtering, and avatar display that works for both LLM models and profiles.

2. **Implemented `ChatLLMModelSelector.vue`** - A new LLM model selector using the Selector component for single selection, moved from the toolbar to before the profile selector in the input area.

3. **Rewrote `ChatProfileSelector.vue`** - Updated to use the shared Selector component for multiple profile selection with filtering capabilities.

4. **Created unified `ChatInputBox.vue`** - New container component that places the LLM model selector before the profile selector, manages the editor, and removed the model selector from the toolbar.

5. **Maintained VueDeveloper profile standards** - All components follow the required structure (setup/template/script), use TailwindCSS and DaisyUI, leverage `$storex` for state management, and avoid unnecessary imports or complexity.

# Conversation Summary

1. **Initial Request**: User asked to create a unified selector component for both LLM models and profiles in a Vue chat application, moving the LLM selector from toolbar to before the profile selector.

2. **Implementation**: Created reusable `Selector.vue` component with text filtering, alphabetical sorting, and support for both single and multiple selection modes, along with wrapper components for LLM models and profiles.

3. **Integration**: Updated `ChatInputBox.vue` and `Chat.vue` to use the new selector components, removing the LLM selector from the toolbar and organizing the input interface with the model selector appearing first.

4. **Full-Width Fix**: Addressed layout issue where selectors weren't displaying at full width by adding `flex-1` classes and restructuring the container layout to allow equal space sharing between model and profile selectors.

5. **Final Result**: Delivered a production-ready solution with consistent VueDeveloper profile structure, DaisyUI components, and responsive grid-based item selection with badges showing active selections.
